text: I had passed the Magic Shop several times before but it was my little son Gip. <break time="0.8s" /> Who finally pulled me over to its window. <break time="0.8s" /> He held my finger tightly. <break time="0.8s" /> And hauled me right up to the glass. <break time="0.8s" /> Where all kinds of tricks. <break time="0.8s" /> Were on display. <break time="0.8s" /> There were magic balls, magic hens. <break time="0.8s" /> Wonderful cones, puppets for ventriloquists. <break time="0.8s" /> And packs of cards. <break time="0.8s" /> That looked quite ordinary. <break time="0.8s" /> If I were rich. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Gip. <break time="0.8s" /> Pointing at the Disappearing Egg. <break time="0.8s" /> I would buy myself that one. <break time="0.8s" /> He also wanted the Crying Baby, Very Human. <break time="0.8s" /> And a mysterious box with a label. <break time="0.8s" /> That said. <break time="0.8s" /> Buy One and Astonish Your Friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Anything vanishes under those cones. <break time="0.8s" /> He told me seriously. <break time="0.8s" /> Because I have read about it in a book. <break time="0.8s" /> He pointed out that the Vanishing Halfpenny was placed upside down. <break time="0.8s" /> So that nobody could see. <break time="0.8s" /> How the trick was done. <break time="0.8s" /> I reminded him that his birthday was less than a hundred days away. <break time="0.8s" /> And he said nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> But held my finger more tightly. <break time="0.8s" /> So we went in and it was not until I was inside. <break time="0.8s" /> That I noticed. <break time="0.8s" /> How strange the little shop really was.
